# What is in a step

A step is one piece of work for an agent: text it reads and follows, and a line saying how to tell that it is done. A workflow is a list of steps. Nothing in a step is run by a computer.

## The fields of a step

| Field | Written | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | by you | What it is called: one line of plain text, shown in lists, in the strip of a run and in terminals. |
| `instructions` | by you | What to do, written for whoever does the work and knows nothing else about it. Plain text or Markdown. `{{task}}` and the other inputs of a run are filled in. |
| `doneWhen` | by you | One line: how to tell that the step is finished. The agent is told to report done when this is true. |
| `needs` | by you | What whoever does it must have and Aubergine does not supply: an MCP server, a command, access to something. Shown before a run, with what the agent's setup has; nothing here is checked or installed. |
| `produces` | by you | What it hands over when it is done: `note` (a few words, which every step can hand over) or `checklist` (a list the next step and you can tick). |
| `kind` | for you | What sort of step it is: `instructions` (text an agent reads and follows) or `approval` (a place where the run stops until a person has decided). Nothing in a step is run by a computer. |
| `ask` | by you | For an approval: what the person is asked to decide, in plain text. It is shown to the person beside the buttons; an approval has no instructions for an agent. |
| `lookAt` | by you | For an approval, if you like: what the person should look at before deciding. |
| `origin` | for you | Where it came from: made here, a template, a file, a draft an agent wrote, a repository. Kept for you to see; nothing is decided by it. |
| `source` | for you | For a copy of a saved step: which step and which of its versions it was copied from, and a mark of the content as copied. From these the editor says whether the copy is unchanged, was changed here, or has a newer version on the shelf. Null for a step that is not such a copy. |
| `id` | for you | Its ID inside its workflow. It stays the same when the step is edited, so that a run can tell which step it is on. You do not write it: it is made for you. |
| `extra` | for you | Fields from a file that this version does not know, kept so that they are written out again. |

## A saved step also has

| Field | Written | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | for you | The number of its newest version. Editing it adds one. |
| `versions` | for you | Its saved versions, oldest first: each with who saved it, when, and a line on what changed. None is ever changed. |
| `state` | for you | `current`, or `retired`: kept and still working where it is used, but not offered when inserting and not run by itself. |
| `replacedBy` | for you | For a retired step: the saved step to use in its place, when one was named. |

A saved step is copied into a workflow, never linked: changing the shelf changes no workflow. A copy remembers where it came from (`source`), so the editor can say when a newer version is on the shelf, and you decide whether to take it.
